title: Initial Experiment with Force-Directed Placement
abstract: This submission moves beyond the static baseline by using a force-directed placement algorithm. It begins with a random distribution of circle centers and iteratively applies repulsion forces to resolve overlaps. After positioning, it computes the maximum possible radii for the resulting configuration.

original_submission.content:
import numpy as np

def construct_packing():
    """
    Constructs a packing of 26 circles using a force-directed layout algorithm
    to position the centers before calculating radii.
    """
    n = 26
    
    # Start with a random configuration, avoiding the edges initially
    np.random.seed(42) # for reproducibility
    centers = np.random.rand(n, 2) * 0.8 + 0.1
    radii = np.full(n, 0.05) # Start with a small, uniform radius for overlap checks

    # Iteratively adjust positions based on overlaps
    for _ in range(250): # More iterations for better settling
        # Repulsion force between overlapping circles
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                delta = centers[j] - centers[i]
                dist_sq = np.sum(delta**2)
                dist = np.sqrt(dist_sq) if dist_sq > 0 else 1e-9
                
                overlap = radii[i] + radii[j] - dist
                
                if overlap > 0:
                    # A simple linear force model
                    force_magnitude = overlap / dist 
                    force_vector = force_magnitude * delta
                    
                    # Apply a fraction of the force to move circles apart
                    centers[i] -= force_vector * 0.1
                    centers[j] += force_vector * 0.1

        # Boundary checks: push circles back from the walls
        for i in range(n):
            centers[i] = np.clip(centers[i], radii[i], 1 - radii[i])

    # After positioning, compute the maximal radii for the final centers
    final_radii = np.zeros(n)
    epsilon = 1e-9
    
    # Limit by distance to square borders
    for i in range(n):
        x, y = centers[i]
        final_radii[i] = min(x, y, 1 - x, 1 - y)
    
    # Iteratively shrink radii to resolve any remaining overlaps
    for _ in range(20):
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                dist = np.linalg.norm(centers[i] - centers[j])
                rad_sum = final_radii[i] + final_radii[j]
                if dist < rad_sum - epsilon:
                    if rad_sum > 0:
                        scale_factor = dist / rad_sum
                        final_radii[i] *= scale_factor
                        final_radii[j] *= scale_factor
    
    return centers, np.maximum(final_radii, 0)
